d.caveats:
1. Computed vs transcribed: every table is computed. Only the per-round mean_unlocks and stone/wood counts in the D5 context line are copied from iter-k.json, and the iter json values are otherwise used only as cross-checks. The GW-L start S accuracy was cross-checked against eval.json, not copied. I did not recompute the WALL-SOLVE 36/37% played and 62/64% kept figures (Z8 games, days 0-3); my round-1 numbers (played 39.3/41.4% policy-only, 36.0/37.9% both; kept 55.2/59.6% both) are on different days and the A27 rule, so are not directly comparable and I do not claim a discrepancy.
2. state.pt is at round 7 on both seeds, so 'current' = r7 (add-on after training on round-7 rows). The games of round k were played by the model after round k-1, so the play-side tables lag the D3 r-labels by one round (D3 r3 = trained through round 3; round-4 games were played by it). Round 8 play is in progress (s200 chunks 0-2 only); not analysed.
3. D5 is played-move agreement, not model top-1 on its own visited states (no per-round checkpoints). D3 uses the fixed labeller-distribution held-out views, which are not the policy's own visited states. Labeller agreement is a proxy for good play, not a score (the labeller is memoryless and scores 8.23 / 7.80 non-habit on the sealed set, per the doc).
4. The 'expected train-mix' random share assumes the buffer sample is uniform; the realised sample (rng state) was not replayed. Row weights in a mixed set are normalised by the mixed set's mean, which I handled in the expectation using raw weights.
5. D2 ALL-played uses all 400 games per round; the loop's own all-played stat used the first 50 games (cross-checked equal on that subset). A row on several kept segments (same event step, several types) takes the largest weight and is classified by that winning segment for D4; ties resolved as imitate.rows_of does.
6. Observations from the numbers (not a causal test): random moves are a small and shrinking part of the training signal (kept 5.9% -> 3.1-3.2% by round 7; weighted 8.8-10.0% -> 3.8-3.9%), and their labeller agreement is chance-level (5-16%), so they are not the main route of erosion. Policy-row quality is what falls: kept policy agreement 58.3/62.6% -> 49.0/46.1% (r1 -> r7), played policy nav agreement 35.6/36.4% -> 18.2/18.3% while played act agreement rises (53.2 -> 68.9 on s200, 61.8 -> 82.4 on s201). Kept rows are 75-83% repeat events (collect_wood and collect_drink repeats dominate), 54-72% of weight; repeat rows agree more with the labeller than first-unlock rows in most rounds, but repeat-policy agreement falls 61.7 -> 50.3 (s200) and 66.8 -> 47.4 (s201). On fixed held-out states map reading degrades monotonically on both seeds (S top-1 -12.3 and -9.8 pts by r7, NLL of the label 0.99 -> 1.84 and 0.95 -> 1.74); entropy first rises at r3 then falls to or below r0 by r7, so the policy is becoming sharper while less correct. The first-pass reading across s200 and s201 is consistent, but only two seeds.
7. Constraints kept: training untouched (not killed, nothing restarted); no repo file edited; no sealed seed or gwls_final.py touched (all world seeds are 1,39x,xxx / 1,398,xxx practice seeds, asserted by practice_seed); torch threads = 1 and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; all output under the diag directory. Note repo code was imported (game.imitate, game.oracle, game.play, game.probe, domain.mode, custom_io) and may have written __pycache__ files next to the repo sources by the interpreter, not by me; no repo source file changed.
